status_reasons: STATUS IS PASS AT THE FLOOR AND THE VALIDATOR WILL WARN THAT IT SHOULD BE READ AS PROVISIONAL — that warning is correct and intended. The piece passes on every axis that can be measured today. Four of RI-PRG06's eight axes (region-1, all-region levels, the Monte Carlo sim, the pace curve) require a world holding at least 891 of its 1,230 hostiles and 269 are placed; the piece's own --census fails closed on exactly that and is right to. Re-open those four when W1-POPULATION and the enemy-roster piece land bodies past the band floor. Nothing in the two hard fails waits on that.
All eight items of the round-1 path to ten were delivered, and six of them I verified independently rather than accepting the status file.
The central charge is answered: arm K kills a live inf_trash with 42 latched `light` swings and no harness kill verb, dying on frame 1421, with a self-break control that never kills.

The re-anchor's band step is genuinely DERIVED, and it survives a harder test than the one round 2 ran: all 18 of §2's band rows recomputed from §3's MARKDOWN roster match, and all six region totals reconcile.
HF-1 is closed to the digit: round 1's projected 2,400,817 x the §7 scale is 1,124,285, RI-PRG06 §1's contract exactly, L93, L120 ratio 2.128 against target 2.13.

HELD AT THE FLOOR — hard fail 1: `loadState('<named>')` does not clear the souls observer, so the class round 2 named in its own status file ('ANY probe in this tree that recycles an encounter is doing the same thing') is unfixed at the boundary. Measured: +384 then +0 across the boundary, same eids, 12 refused re-arms, zero rests. It has already cost tools/progression/critic-souls-r1.mjs three false reds.

HELD AT THE FLOOR — hard fail 2: a partly-cleared population post is released as DORMANT and re-materialised under its stable tag, so five live, full-HP, hostile bodies are worth 0 souls while the sixth beside them pays 64. RI-PRG06 §4's row is 'Respawned enemy x1.00'.

The anchor's remaining un-derived step is worth 1.52x: 12,665/93 is the mean over ALL 93 R1 bodies (36% of the souls from 3% of the bodies) pinned to a TRASH statblock at premium 1.0, against §3's own R1 trash mean of 89.61.

And it lands on the item's zero row: the placed tier-1 mean kill is 38.00, which at §7's 199-body region 1 is 7,562 souls -> L10, where RI-PRG06 method 1 scores 0 at 'outside 11-17'. Nothing asserts it — --check is a range test and --census is fail-closed.
The census scale is keyed to a planning constant and nothing binds it to what is placed; the fail-closed guard opens at 891 bodies, where the scale error is 28%.
The L120 guard — the axis round 1 returned the piece on — is printed by --census in both branches and asserted in neither.
RI-PRG06 method 6 has never had an instrument, and the item's own published bands overlap by up to 76% against its 25% ceiling. Filed as AQ-1 and NOT charged to the piece.

hard_fails.title: the class was named and not fixed: loadState('<named>') does not clear the souls observer
hard_fails.evidence: reports/critic-souls-r2.json arms.C4 — pass1 +384, pass2 +0, same_eids true, refused_rearms 12, hearth_rests 0, after_observer_reset +384, with_unique_tag +384
hard_fails.why_it_matters: applyNamedState() is the scenario boundary every probe in this tree uses. It empties sim.entities and re-seeds stealth and population immediately afterwards for exactly this reason; sim.souls is not in that list, so the epoch gate silently zeroes payment for any probe that recycles eids. Round 2 discovered this face of the bug itself (15/15 -> 8/15) and fixed its own instrument with unique tags. tools/progression/critic-souls-r1.mjs already reports three false reds.

hard_fails.title: a partly-cleared post comes back as live enemies worth zero souls
hard_fails.evidence: reports/critic-souls-r2.json arms.C5 — killed 5 of 6 (+320); released; same tag -> same eids; 6 alive on return, 5 recycled at full hp; killing those 5 paid +0 while the never-killed sixth paid +64
hard_fails.why_it_matters: world/population.js marks a post CLEARED only when every body is down, releases a non-cleared post as DORMANT, and re-materialises it with { tag: p.id } — a stable tag. So the ordinary act of partly clearing a road post, walking 260 m away and coming back produces live, dangerous, killable bodies that pay nothing until the player happens to rest. RI-PRG06 §4's modifier row is 'Respawned enemy x1.00'. PopulationSystem's own CLEARED state already prevents the farm the gate was written for, so the gate is belt-and-braces that mis-fires.

biggest_gap.what: SoulsSystem._alive is keyed on the eid and nothing in the build is authorised to clear it. One bug, two faces: every probe in this tree (HF-1) and every player (HF-2). Both were produced by the round-2 epoch gate, which is otherwise a correct and well-evidenced fix.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The probe face silently under-reports payment for any instrument that recycles an encounter, which round 2 measured as taking its own suite from 15/15 to 8/15 and which has already cost a second tool three false failures — this project rates a probe that quietly reports the wrong number below no probe at all. The player face makes real, dangerous combat unpaid in ordinary play and violates RI-PRG06 §4's own modifier row.
biggest_gap.not_a_hard_fail_because: n/a — it is recorded as two hard fails above. It is not an automatic fail under RI-PRG06's Scoring table, which reserves those for S9 level-scaling and quest souls, both of which are clean.

remedy.action: (1) In engine.js applyNamedState(), beside the existing stealth and population re-seeds: `if (this.sim.souls) this.sim.souls.reset();`. (2) In sim/souls.js, stop keying the gate on the eid alone — have spawnEncounter stamp a spawn generation on the entity and record `{ alive, paidEpoch, gen }`, re-arming when the generation moves OR the rest epoch moves. That keeps round 1's HF-3 farm shut while restoring §4's x1.00 to a body that was genuinely built again.
remedy.acceptance: Two arms in souls-consumption.mjs, neither able to pass while the other fails under a delete-the-fix. (a) An UNTAGGED fight, killed, crossed over loadState('<named>'), killed again, must pay both times. (b) A post of n bodies with n-1 killed, despawned wholesale and re-spawned under the SAME tag, must pay for all n-1 recycled bodies on the second visit AND must still pay nothing for a body that was never despawned and never rested past. tools/progression/critic-souls-r2.mjs arms C4 and C5 are those two arms.

biggest_gap.evidence_note: arms.C4 (+384 then +0 across loadState, 12 refused re-arms, 0 rests) and arms.C5 (5 live full-HP hostiles paid +0 while the never-killed sixth paid +64).

arbitration_questions.question: §2 states its bands are 'deliberately non-overlapping at the edges so that am I in the right region is answerable from a single kill', and method 6 caps adjacent trash-band overlap at 25% of the lower band's width. The published bands overlap by 32.3%, 50.0%, 53.3%, 76.1% and 70.0%. Since §2's bands are exactly the min and max of §3's roster (proved in this verdict), the two cannot be reconciled without moving §3's values, which §7 froze and §1's cumulative column depends on. Does §2's separation claim, method 6's threshold, or §3's spread yield?

arbitration_questions.question: Is world.enemy_census a plan or a measurement? The soul values are derived from it as though it were a fact about the shipped world, while --census tests the shipped world against it. Both cannot be true, and the answer decides whether re-running derive-soul-values.mjs is a maintenance task or a contract violation.

notes: Round 2 is a good round that is held at the pass floor by a regression of its own making. The eight-item path to ten was delivered in full, the central charge is answered with a real fight and a self-break, and the number the piece was returned on is closed to the digit. What holds it at 6 is that the epoch gate — a correct and well-evidenced fix — is keyed on the eid, and the builder found one face of that (its own suite) and named the class in its own status file ('ANY probe in this tree that recycles an encounter is doing the same thing') without fixing it at the boundary where it lives. The other face is worse and nobody had looked: five live, full-HP, hostile bodies worth nothing to a player who partly cleared a road post and came back. Separately, the brief's central question has a split answer worth carrying forward — the BAND step of the re-anchor is genuinely arithmetic and I proved it from the markdown rather than the JSON, but the ANCHOR step is not: 12,665/93 is the mean of a region that includes its boss, pinned to a trash statblock, and the 1.52x that follows lands the placed region 1 on this item's own zero row with no assertion anywhere that would notice.
